note:
Paper 88, Team 38996. Nineteen measured regions over nine of the twenty-one pages, all
nineteen accounted for: eleven figure rows, five table rows, three exclusions, so unaccounted is
zero and nothing is left unresolved. The paper numbers ten figures and six tables; Table 1, the
"process of calculation of weighting process", prints on p9 as a run of text with no rules, owns no
measured region at all, and is declared as a gap rather than invented.

The one structural finding is on p18. Figure 8 is a single system-dynamics diagram - three dotted
cluster boxes labelled Society, Economic and Environment & Resources, twenty-three boxes in all,
joined by arrows carrying plus and minus polarity signs - but the region pass measures FOUR regions
there, because the three sub-graphs are pasted as their own bitmaps inside the outer vector drawing.
The 0.29-area vector region holds the whole diagram and is the exhibit; the three raster pieces
repeat clusters already inside it, so they are excluded as duplicates. That is the first time in
this lane that a single figure arrives as one drawing wrapped around three copies of itself.

What the pictures show, read off the crops. Figure 1 is the index system as a four-level tree,
ending in circles that break every indicator name mid-word and printing "Education" twice as a
Level 2 box. Figure 2 and Figure 3 are the same idea twice: the first is a construction in the
SE/ER plane with both axes ticked only at 0 and 1, one red ideal ray, one black actual vector, a
theta arc, four year markers 2009-2012 squeezed into an unreadable cluster, and rotated ray labels
that collide with the arc; the second throws the axes away and keeps only the rays and the angle.
Figures 4 and 5 are country trajectories in that plane with the legend outside at the right, and
the paper labels each path with 2003 and 2012 only, printing "2012" twice inside America's. Figure 6
is an ARIMA forecast whose two confidence bands are keyed only in the sentence above it.

Figures 7, 9 and 10 are the paper's quantitative evidence and they are thin: Figure 7 is two pasted
column charts over the same twenty-two index numbers with different y windows, neither axis titled,
and about a quarter of the bars at exactly zero; Figures 9 and 10 share an axis frame with no axis
titles and no units at all, Figure 9 puts two series in it and Figure 10 four, and in Figure 10 the
four programmes sit on top of each other until the last third of the window, which is where the
paper's conclusion is supposed to come from.

The tables are where the paper's arithmetic is legible, and where its labels fail. Table 2 is
transposed - countries across, one measure down - and prints two distances in red with no key.
Table 3 is nine little grey boxes in three rows in index order though the prose calls it a ranking,
with the last cell empty and no header row. Table 4 carries the plan's judgement in five words per
row and colours the one rejection red with no legend. Table 5 is three unrelated lists of estimated
equations side by side, five and ten and eight of them, wrapping onto unindented continuation
lines. Table 6 compares four proposals whose distances agree to the fourth decimal place in three
of the four years, so the ranking it is meant to support is not visible in its own numbers.

Citation is regular on this paper, which is worth recording because it is unusual here: every
numbered figure and every measured table is named in the prose. Figure 7 and Table 5 are named a
page before they print, Table 6 a page before its grid, and Figure 2 is named a page after it -
once, parenthetically - while Tables 2, 3 and 4 and Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are named on
their own pages. The one grid never mentioned is Table 1, the one grid with no measured region.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: nineteen measured regions resolve into eleven figure rows, five table rows and three exclusions, with nothing unaccounted [place.area_frac].

A drawing whose sub-graphs are pasted as separate bitmaps counts once: the 0.29-area vector region on p18 holds the whole of Figure 8, and the three raster pieces inside it repeat clusters that are already in that drawing, so they are excluded as duplicates rather than recorded as further rows [place.area_frac].

Two measured panels under one printed caption are two rows with one shared verbatim: Figure 7 prints its sensitivity bars in an upper and a lower panel, pasted apart, and both rows carry 'Figure 7 Sensitivity of each index' [caption.verbatim].
A caption that prints no colon is numbered 'Figure N' or 'Table N' and not 'Figure N:'; every caption on this paper is set that way [caption.numbering].
A caption printed under the data rows is position 'below' even when the words precede the grid in the text layer's own reading order, as Table 2's does [caption.position].

A construction with real index axes is line even when it plots almost nothing: Figure 2 draws rays and an angle in the SE/ER plane with both axes ticked, so it takes the plot families [geometry.family].

A construction with no axes and no data is other, and it is the only other row on the paper: Figure 3 is five grey rays, one red ideal ray and four angle labels, set in the model section rather than beside the results [place.section_kind].
A tree of labelled boxes and circles is flowchart-or-schematic, and the four-level index system of Figure 1 is that family with no numbers anywhere [geometry.family].

An outside legend is recorded as outside-right and not as inside: Figures 4, 5, 9 and 10 and both Figure 7 panels carry their key to the right of the plot, which is the only legend placement this paper uses [geometry.legend].

A chart whose axes print no titles is recorded with printed_numbers true and the missing titles named in the note: Figures 9 and 10 print tick values on both axes and no axis titles at all [geometry.printed_numbers].
A confidence band keyed only by prose is legend 'none': Figure 6's grey and light blue bands are named in the sentence above the figure and nowhere in the art [geometry.legend].

Rows are counted as printed and columns physically: Table 2 prints one data row across five country columns, Table 3 prints three rows of number-name pairs in nine cells, Table 5 prints three unrelated lists side by side [table.rows].
A merged band over a group of judgement columns makes merged_cells true even when no cell spans two rows, as Table 4's 'Actual Requirement' header does [table.merged_cells].

A grid whose only rules are horizontal is booktabs, and a grid whose small cells are each closed by vertical strokes is boxed: Table 3's grey index cells are the only boxed grid here [table.rule_style].
A colour code printed with no key is recorded as a defect, not as a legend: Table 2's two red distances and Table 4's red and green decisions both carry their meaning only in prose [table.zebra].
An exhibit first named on an earlier page takes a positive lead_pages: Figure 7 and Table 5 are both named a page before they print, and Table 6 a page before its grid [mention.lead_pages].
An exhibit whose pointer sits a page after the art takes a negative lead_pages: Figure 2 is printed on p10 and first named on p11 as '(Figure 2)' [mention.lead_pages].
A pointer written parenthetically is recorded with lead_pattern parenthetical and the parenthesised spelling quoted as printed [mention.lead_pattern].

tables.note: Three columns headed Economic Subsystem, Society Subsystem and Environment & Resources Subsystem, holding five, ten and eight estimated equations respectively - the columns do not share rows, so the printed grid is a sheet of three independent lists rather than a table with records. Rules above the header and below the last row only, nothing between rows. Every equation is linear in its regressors with coefficients to four decimals: I = -4.1019 + 0.0804 CRW, M = -31.7202 + 0.3703 LFPR + 0.0949 RSEC, POP = POP/1000 (BR - DR), NOE = 1858.4 - 14.3 CRW, and so on. Long equations wrap onto continuation lines with no hanging indent, so an equation can read as two rows; the wrapped lines in the environment column carry a small negative indent that reads as misalignment.

The four proposals differ in the fourth decimal place in every year except 2030, where the last column switches between five and six decimals and the differences are still under 0.03, so the table cannot support a ranking on the evidence it prints; the caption's 'every five year' is the paper's own grammar.
